question: In the morning the vineyard counted 150 bearing vines, then found 20 more in the lower field and 8 along the fence. In the afternoon each vine gave 5 bunches, and each bunch weighed 8 ounces. In the evening 4704 ounces were pressed for juice. How many ounces of grapes remain?

A student had 171 pages to read. They subtracted 12 for skipped sections (morning). They added 41 (afternoon). They multiplied by 9 for related readings. They multiplied by 6 for semester material. Lisa had 500 pages assigned but different. After subtracting and adding morning material but before multiplication, how many pages to cover?

In the morning a parking garage had 162 cars in it. By mid-morning 33 more cars had arrived, and another 51 arrived during the afternoon. In the late afternoon 110 cars drove out. In the evening 93 more cars left. How many cars were in the garage at the end of the evening?

A business had 159 dollars (morning). They multiplied by 5 for growth. They subtracted 430 for large investment (afternoon). They subtracted 81 for overhead. They subtracted 110 more (evening, using 'double' and 'minutes to hours'). Tom and Lisa made decisions (named). After multiplication but before investment subtraction, how much money in the mid-morning state?

A student had 30 minutes. They subtracted 2 for setup (morning). They added 57 for extension (afternoon). They subtracted 28 for lunch. They divided by 3 for group work. They added 45 more minutes (evening). The school day lasted 360 minutes but this was separate. After all morning and afternoon activities but before the evening division, how much time in minutes?

In the morning, Chen made 207 portions of noodles and then made a second batch of exactly the same size, doubling his stock, while Wei's stall next door had 350 portions. By midday Chen had sold 113 portions. In the afternoon a helper brought 17 more portions. Chen packed 6 dumplings with every portion still on the stall. In the evening he divided all those dumplings equally into 6 boxes. How many dumplings are in the first box?

A cinema has 9 screens, each with 7 rows of 45 seats, and it runs 8 shows a day on every screen. On Saturday half of all the seats across all the day's shows were sold. A private booking then added 45 more tickets. Every ticket sold for 5 dollars. The cinema opened 12 years ago. How many dollars did the cinema take in on Saturday?

In the morning Mia picked 109 strawberries, then 19 more after a short break and another 43 before lunch, and she divided the whole pick equally into 3 punnets. In the afternoon she ate 43 strawberries out of one punnet over half an hour. In the evening she decided that what was left in that punnet was the perfect size for a market punnet, and she planned to pack 9 punnets of that size on each of 4 market days. How many strawberries will Mia need for those 4 market days?

In the morning the bakery received 182 boxes of eggs with 6 eggs in each, plus 37 loose eggs, which the cook checked twice. In the afternoon the farm sent 35 more eggs. In the evening every egg went into the pancake batter, and each egg makes 4 pancakes. How many pancakes did the bakery make?

A warehouse had 204 boxes initially. They removed 41 boxes for shipment. They added 15 boxes from returns. They multiplied by 9 to track total inventory. They removed 223 boxes for a big order. They removed 911 boxes for a bulk sale. They removed 63 more boxes for warehouse closure. How many boxes were left?

Ines gathered 95 walnuts from the tree at the end of the lane, and her brother Rafael added 40 that he had picked, fewer than Ines had found. They tipped them all together and shared them equally among 5 cloth bags. Ines took one bag home and cracked every walnut in it into 4 pieces. She threw away 11 pieces that had gone mouldy inside the shell. Each remaining piece was then chopped into 4 crumbs for a cake topping. How many crumbs did Ines end up with?

Two partners, Frank and Emma, compared stores. Frank's store started with 186 items. He added 31 from a transfer. He added 22 from a donation. He added 24 more from inventory. He doubled for promotion pricing. Emma managed another location. One distractor: the warehouse had 75 items. How many items in Frank's store for promotion?

Sarah has 98 apples. After selling 73 apples at the farmers market, she had triple the remaining amount picked by her friend. Then she sold 75 more and ended with 6 times that amount from another harvest. How many apples does Sarah have in total?

In the morning, a shop had 38 items. They added 12. They removed 25. They added 37. They had a distractor of 50 items. They added 5. By afternoon, they multiplied by 7. By evening, they removed 34. How many items?
A team had 216 members initially. This was divided by 3. This was tripled. Then tripled again. She added 43. She removed 187. Her partner team had 95 members. What was the total?

A charity had 156 minutes of phone calls to make, more than two and a half hours, and shared the work equally among 3 volunteers. Tam received her share, and then 17 minutes of calls were added to her list. Her friend Uli finished his calls sooner than Tam. Tam spread her calls equally over 3 days. On Monday she added 59 minutes of extra calls, and then 23 minutes of her Monday calls were cancelled. How many minutes of calls did Tam make on Monday?

A business operates through the day. They start with 184 dollars in the morning. They lose 80 dollars to opening costs. They double by 2 through morning sales. They add 59 dollars from additional revenue. They add 76 dollars from other sources. They add 15 dollars in interest. Converting to dollars, what is their daily total?

In the morning Hiro's team packed 142 cartons with 8 jars in each, and half of the jars were sold at the early market. In the afternoon the remaining jars were split equally among 4 shops, and the first shop calls its share the shelf stock. In the evening the first shop received 63 more jars for its shelf stock. Hiro's rival Sato sold fewer jars than Hiro. How many jars are in the first shop's shelf stock?

A toy factory produced 148 boxes of action figures in one run. Each box actually contained enough figures to fill 4 retail boxes once repackaged, multiplying the total. A shipping error then meant 405 boxes had to be pulled for relabeling. A separate quality check removed another 183 boxes for defects. A different production line, unrelated to this batch, made 700 boxes that same day. Finally, a returned shipment added 10 more boxes back to the count. How many boxes were left in this batch's count?

A base value was 221. By morning, it multiplied by 6 (groups). By midday, it multiplied by 4 more (24x total). By afternoon, 1034 were removed. By evening, it tripled. Finally, 28 were added. Her coworker had 150. How many final?

A comic book warehouse had 149 crates of comics ready for distribution. The manager mentioned that a dozen forklifts were being serviced that week, though that had nothing to do with the crate count. A regional recall required sending back 26 crates to the printer. A restocking order then turned every crate into 6 crates. A second restocking order turned each of those into 9 crates. A final bulk order turned every crate into 6 more crates. How many crates of comics were in the warehouse after the final bulk order?
A warehouse had 206 boxes. They added 15, reaching 221. They tripled to 663. They expanded 6 times to 3,978. They doubled to 7,956. They removed 3,524, leaving 4,432 boxes. How many boxes remain?

An orchard had 207 apple trees initially. They multiplied the count 6 times through planting expansion. Then they added 44 newly planted trees. They subtracted 697 trees due to land sale. They multiplied by 9 for a future projection calculation. They added 61 more saplings. The neighboring farm had 1000 trees but this was separate. After multiplication and before the land sale, how many trees did they have (express as a word quantity where appropriate)?

A city tracked the total number of bicycles available at the downtown bike-share station, starting with 209 bicycles at dawn. A morning delivery added 4 more bicycles. During the morning commute, 69 bicycles were checked out and not returned. A midday delivery added 7 more bicycles. Finally, an expansion event multiplied the station's tracked bicycle count by 5. How many bicycles did the tracked station show after the expansion?

In the morning, Aiden has 94 dollars saved in his desk drawer, which he always mentally counts as 9,400 cents just for fun. By midday, he earns 79 more dollars from mowing lawns around the neighborhood. In the early afternoon, he spends 102 dollars on a new bike helmet and lock. His sister Zoe, who has been saving separately, has only 60 dollars in her own jar, far behind her brother's total. By late afternoon, a matching bonus from his parents brings his savings to 5 times what remained after the bike purchase. That evening, a second matching bonus from his grandparents brings his total to 5 times what it had grown to. How much money does Aiden have saved by the end of the day?
